name: Job Hunting
title: Offer Hunter
blurb: Getting into a Japanese consulting firm means passing ES screening, web tests, video interviews and group discussions in the 就活 system, often before any case or technical interview.

chapters.title: Japan's new-graduate hiring flow
chapters.read: Read a 就活 guidebook's opening chapters and your university career centre's materials for international students on 新卒一括採用, インターンシップ, 説明会, ES, web tests, interviews, 内々定 and 内定, plus the visa change after an offer. Key idea: the order of steps and the alternative routes (通年採用, autumn entry) for non-April graduates.
chapters.produce: Draw your own hiring-flow map with target firms in each of your three role types and the route each one offers (new-grad, year-round, internship-linked), and book one career-centre consultation.

quiz.q: What is 新卒一括採用?
opts: Hiring only experienced mid-career workers
Companies hiring a cohort of graduating students together each year, usually with a common start date
Hiring part-time students for one summer
A government exam for public-sector jobs
quiz.ex: 新卒 = new graduates, 一括 = all at once. Many Japanese firms recruit graduates as a batch, often joining together in spring.

quiz.q: What is the difference between 内々定 and 内定?
opts: 内々定 is a rejection; 内定 is an offer
内々定 is for part-time jobs; 内定 is for full-time jobs
There is no difference; they are spelling variants
内々定 is an informal offer given before the formal offer; 内定 is the formal offer of employment
quiz.ex: Firms often give an informal 内々定 first and confirm it later as a formal 内定, typically with a written offer.

quiz.q: Which order best shows the typical new-graduate selection flow?
opts: Entry and company briefings -> ES and web test -> several interview rounds -> offer
Offer -> interviews -> ES -> entry
Interviews -> entry -> web test -> ES
Web test -> offer -> ES -> company briefings
quiz.ex: You register (entry) and attend 説明会, submit an ES and take an aptitude test, then pass several interviews before an offer.

quiz.q: Why are internships important in Japanese job hunting?
opts: They are legally required before any job offer
They replace the need for any interview
They let you learn about the firm, and at some companies they connect to early selection routes
They are only for students who have already received an offer
quiz.ex: Internships give insight and contacts, and some firms invite strong interns into early (早期) selection. Policies differ by firm.

quiz.q: What is 通年採用 and why can it matter for a student graduating in August?
opts: Year-round hiring, which lets students with non-standard graduation dates apply outside the usual cycle
Hiring that only happens in April
Hiring only for students from Japanese high schools
A system where students work one year before applying
quiz.ex: 通年 = all year. Year-round or autumn-entry routes suit graduates who finish outside the March cycle, such as international students.

quiz.q: An international student on a 留学 (student) visa receives a full-time job offer. What usually needs to happen before starting work?
opts: Nothing; a student visa allows full-time work after graduation
Leave Japan and apply for a tourist visa
Get a 内定 from a second company
Change the status of residence to a working status that fits the job
quiz.ex: The student status of residence does not cover full-time employment; the student applies to change to a suitable working status, usually with the employer's support.

chapters.title: Aptitude tests: SPI, 玉手箱, TG-WEB
chapters.read: Work through an SPI 問題集 (言語 and 非言語) and a 玉手箱 / TG-WEB 問題集, focusing on 損益算, 速さ, 割合, 仕事算, 四則逆算, 図表の読み取り and 数列. Key idea: speed comes from recognising the question type instantly.
chapters.produce: Complete two full timed mock tests for each of SPI and 玉手箱, log your error types, and redo every missed question until you can solve it in under one minute.

quiz.q: What are the main parts of the SPI?
opts: Only an English essay
Ability tests (言語 = verbal, 非言語 = non-verbal/numerical) and a personality test
A physical fitness test and a typing test
Only a group discussion
quiz.ex: SPI combines verbal and non-verbal ability sections with a personality questionnaire; some versions add English or structural-thinking parts.

quiz.q: SPI style (損益算): An item costs ¥2,000 to buy. The shop sets the list price at a 30% markup, then sells it at 10% off the list price. What is the profit in yen?
SPI style (速さ): A and B start 15 km apart and walk toward each other, A at 4 km/h and B at 6 km/h. After how many minutes do they meet?
quiz.ex: Closing speed = 4 + 6 = 10 km/h. 15 / 10 = 1.5 hours = 90 minutes.

quiz.q:
玉手箱 style (四則逆算): Find the value of □.
□ × 0.25 + 12 = 30

TG-WEB style (数列): What number comes next?
2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
quiz.ex: The differences are 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12: 30 + 12 = 42. (Each term is n x (n+1).)

quiz.q: What is a well-known feature of 玉手箱's ability sections?
opts: There is no time limit at all
Each question is a 30-minute essay
Each section uses one question format repeated many times under a tight time limit
All questions are oral, answered to an interviewer
quiz.ex: Because one format repeats within a section (e.g. all 図表の読み取り), recognising the format and working fast is the key skill.

chapters.title: エントリーシート in English and Japanese
chapters.read: Read an ES-writing guide's chapters on 志望動機, 自己PR and ガクチカ, and the English-resume section of your career centre's guide. Key ideas: 結論ファースト, specific evidence, consistent style (です・ます or である), and respecting character limits.
chapters.produce: Write a 400字 志望動機 and a 400字 自己PR in Japanese, plus a 200-word English version of each, and get them reviewed by a career-centre adviser or a Japanese friend.

quiz.q: What makes a strong 志望動機 (reason for applying)?
opts: It praises the company's size and famous brand only
It links your own experience and goals to what this specific company does and why it, not a competitor
It explains that the salary is high
It is the same text used for every company
quiz.ex: Reviewers look for fit: why this industry, why this firm, and how your background connects to its work.

quiz.q: An ES question has a 400字以内 limit. Which answer length is best?
opts: About 100 characters, to look concise
About 450 characters, to show enthusiasm
About 200 characters, exactly half
About 360-400 characters
quiz.ex: Using most of the limit shows effort and gives room for evidence; going over the limit breaks the rule.

quiz.q: How should you handle sentence style (文体) in a Japanese ES?
opts: Choose です・ます調 or である調 and use it consistently
Mix both styles to show variety
Use casual speech (だよ, だね) to sound friendly
Change style in every paragraph
quiz.ex: Either style can be accepted, but mixing them looks careless.

quiz.q: Which English ES sentence is strongest?
opts: I was responsible for various tasks in a team.
I am a hard-working and passionate person.
Led a five-person team that cut event costs by 20% by renegotiating venue contracts.
Participated in a club and did many things.
quiz.ex: It starts with an action verb, shows your role, gives a measurable result and explains how.

quiz.q: What does 結論ファースト mean when writing an ES answer?
opts: Start with your childhood and build up to the answer
Put the conclusion only in the last sentence
Avoid giving any conclusion
Start with the direct answer to the question, then give the reasons and evidence
quiz.ex: Readers screen many ESs quickly; the first sentence should answer the question (e.g. 「私の強みは〇〇です。」).

quiz.q: What is the difference between 自己PR and ガクチカ?
opts: 自己PR presents your strength and how it helps the company; ガクチカ describes what you put effort into as a student and how you acted
They are identical questions
自己PR is about your family; ガクチカ is about your hobbies
自己PR is only for engineers; ガクチカ is only for business roles
quiz.ex: The same episode can support both, but 自己PR centres on the strength, while ガクチカ centres on the effort, process and learning.

chapters.title: STAR stories and ガクチカ
chapters.read: Study an interview-preparation guide's section on behavioural questions and STAR, and a Japanese guide's chapter on ガクチカ and 深掘り questions. Key ideas: most time on Action, clear personal role, measurable Result, and why you made each choice.
chapters.produce: Build a bank of five STAR stories (leadership, teamwork, failure, problem solving, working across cultures), each with a 1-minute English and 1-minute Japanese version, and answer five 'why?' follow-ups for each.

quiz.q: What does STAR stand for?
opts: Strength, Team, Ambition, Reason
Situation, Task, Action, Result
Story, Timing, Answer, Reflection
Summary, Target, Approach, Review
quiz.ex: STAR is a structure for behavioural answers: the context, your goal, what you did, and what happened.

quiz.q: Which part of a STAR answer should usually take the most time?
opts: Situation
Task
Action
Small talk before the story
quiz.ex: Interviewers want to see what you personally did and how you thought, so the Action part deserves the most detail.

quiz.q: You tell a team story and keep saying 'we did this, we did that'. What is the problem?
opts: The interviewer cannot tell what you personally did
Using 'we' is rude in English
It makes the story too short
There is no problem; you should never say 'I'
quiz.ex: Credit the team, but make your own decisions and actions clear with 'I'.

quiz.q: What do Japanese interviewers mainly look for in a ガクチカ?
opts: Only how famous or large the activity was
Whether you won a national prize
How many different activities you joined
How you think and act, which they expect you to repeat at work (再現性)
quiz.ex: A modest activity told with clear reasoning and effort beats an impressive title with no detail about your process.

quiz.q: After your ガクチカ, the interviewer asks 「なぜその方法を選んだのですか。」 What should you prepare?
opts: A longer version of the same story
A different, unrelated story
The reason behind each key decision, including other options you considered
An apology for choosing that method
quiz.ex: 深掘り (digging-deeper) questions test whether your actions were thought through. Know the 'why' behind each step.

quiz.q: Which Result statement is best?
opts: It went quite well, I think.
Club membership grew from 20 to 32 in one semester, and the new recruiting process is still used.
Everyone was happy.
We tried our best until the end.
quiz.ex: A good Result is concrete and, where possible, measurable, and shows lasting impact.

chapters.title: HireVue and video interviews
chapters.read: Read the candidate guide that video-interview platforms and employers publish, and your career centre's notes on recorded interviews. Key ideas: one-way recorded answers, prep time and answer time limits, camera, light, sound, and short answer-first structure.
chapters.produce: Record yourself answering ten common questions (five in English, five in Japanese) with a 30-second prep and 60-second answer limit, then review and re-record your three weakest answers.

quiz.q: What is a one-way (recorded) video interview such as HireVue?
opts: A live video call with a panel of interviewers
You record answers to questions shown on screen, without a live interviewer, usually with set preparation and answer times
A written test taken on paper at the company
A phone call from a recruiter
quiz.ex: The questions appear on screen; you record answers within time limits and the company reviews them later.

quiz.q: Where should you look while answering?
opts: At your own image on the screen
At notes on the desk
Into the camera lens
Out of the window to think
quiz.ex: Looking at the lens reads as eye contact to the viewer.

quiz.q: You have 60 seconds to answer 'Tell us about yourself'. Which structure fits best?
opts: Your full life story from childhood
A list of every course you took
Silence for 30 seconds, then a quick sentence
One-sentence summary, one specific example, then a link to the role
quiz.ex: Short limits need answer-first structure and one strong example.

quiz.q: How should your lighting be set up?
opts: Main light in front of you, facing your face
A bright window directly behind you
No light so the background is hidden
A single light directly above your head only
quiz.ex: Front lighting shows your face clearly; a bright light behind you turns you into a silhouette.

quiz.q: The platform offers a practice question before the real ones. What is the best use of it?
opts: Skip it to save time
Use it to ask the company questions
Check your camera, microphone, framing and timing
Record your real answer to every question in it
quiz.ex: Practice questions are usually not assessed; use them to fix technical and pacing problems before the real questions.

quiz.q: Which speaking style works best in a recorded interview?
opts: Clear, slightly slower than usual, with the conclusion first
As fast as possible to fit more content
Reading a script word for word off the screen
Very quiet, to sound calm
quiz.ex: Reviewers cannot ask you to repeat yourself, so clarity and structure matter more than volume of content.

chapters.title: Group discussions (グループディスカッション)
chapters.read: Read a 就活 guide's chapter on グループディスカッション and watch public example GD videos. Key ideas: roles (司会, 書記, タイムキーパー), the flow (define the goal, generate ideas, set criteria, decide, present), and contributing to the team's result.
chapters.produce: Take part in at least three practice GDs (career centre or study group), and after each one write down your contributions, one phrase you used well and one you want to add.

quiz.q: What is the タイムキーパー's role in a GD?
opts: Write down everyone's ideas
Manage the time plan and tell the group when to move to the next step
Present the conclusion to the evaluators
Decide the final answer alone
quiz.ex: The time keeper keeps the group on schedule so there is time to conclude and present. The 書記 takes notes.

quiz.q: What do evaluators mainly look for in a GD?
opts: Who speaks the most
Who disagrees with everyone
Who uses the most difficult vocabulary
How each person helps the team reach a good conclusion
quiz.ex: Contribution to the team's output, logic and cooperation matter more than airtime.

quiz.q: What should the group usually do first?
opts: Vote on the final answer
Write the presentation
Agree on the goal and define unclear terms in the theme (前提の定義)
Split up and work alone
quiz.ex: Defining the goal and key terms first stops the group from talking past each other later.

quiz.q: One member is dominating and another has not spoken. What is the best move?
opts: Summarise the current point and invite the quiet member, e.g. 「〇〇さんはどう思われますか。」
Stay silent to avoid conflict
Tell the dominant member to stop talking
Start a separate discussion with the quiet member
quiz.ex: Drawing others in politely improves the team's output and shows facilitation skills.

quiz.q: The theme is 「売上を2倍にする施策を考えてください」. The group has many ideas. What should it do before choosing?
opts: Pick the first idea mentioned
Agree on evaluation criteria such as impact and feasibility
Keep adding ideas until time runs out
Choose the idea of the person who talked most
quiz.ex: Explicit criteria make the choice logical and easy to explain in the presentation.

quiz.q: A 40-minute GD is planned as: 10% defining the goal, 40% generating ideas, 30% evaluating, and the rest summarising and preparing the presentation. How many minutes are left for summarising and preparing?

boss.q: SPI style (割合): A university has 300 students. 40% belong to a club, and 25% of club members belong to two clubs. How many students belong to two clubs?
boss.ex: Club members = 300 x 0.4 = 120. Two clubs = 120 x 0.25 = 30.

boss.q: SPI style (仕事算): A can finish a job alone in 12 days and B in 6 days. How many days does it take them working together?
boss.ex: A does 1/12 a day, B 1/6 a day. Together 1/12 + 2/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 a day, so 4 days.

boss.q:
玉手箱 style (四則逆算): Find □.
48 ÷ □ = 0.6
SPI style (濃度): Mix 200 g of 10% salt water with 300 g of 5% salt water. What is the concentration of the mixture, in %?
Arin graduates at the end of August. Which hiring routes fit this timing best?
opts: Only routes that require graduation in March
Only mid-career hiring that requires several years of work experience
Waiting a full year before applying anywhere
Year-round hiring (通年採用) and autumn-entry positions, plus regular new-graduate routes that accept non-March graduates
boss.ex: Many firms accept non-March graduates through year-round or autumn entry; checking each firm's eligibility for the expected graduation date is the key step.

boss.q:
In this answer, which sentence is the Task?
(1) 'Our club's membership had fallen for two years.' (2) 'As vice-captain, I was asked to raise sign-ups by 50%.' (3) 'I redesigned our recruitment events around trial practices.' (4) 'Sign-ups rose 60%.'
opts: Sentence (1)
Sentence (3)
Sentence (2)
Sentence (4)
boss.ex: (1) is the Situation, (2) the Task (your goal or responsibility), (3) the Action and (4) the Result.

boss.q: In a GD with 15 minutes left, the group has listed ten ideas but has not decided anything. What is the best contribution?
opts: Suggest five more ideas
Restart by redefining the theme from zero
Wait silently for the facilitator to decide
Propose two criteria, score the ideas quickly, and agree on one to present
boss.ex: With limited time, converging with clear criteria secures a conclusion the group can defend.

boss.q: A HireVue question asks: 'Why this company, and what would you do in your first year?' How should you answer?
opts: Answer both parts in order, briefly signposting each ('First, why this company... Second, in my first year...')
Answer only the first part in depth
Answer only the part you prepared for
Ask the camera to repeat the question
boss.ex: Signposting shows you heard both parts and makes the answer easy to follow without a live interviewer.

boss.q: What is the best order for a 400字 ガクチカ?
opts: 学び -> 結果 -> 行動 -> 課題 -> 結論
結論 (what you did) -> 課題 (the problem) -> 行動 (your actions and why) -> 結果 (results) -> 学び (what you learned and how you will use it)
Background only, with no result
結果 -> 結論, with no actions
boss.ex: Answer-first, then problem, actions, results and learning: the same logic as STAR with a lesson at the end.

boss.q: What is a 内定承諾書?
opts: A rejection letter from the company
A certificate of passing the SPI
An application form for an internship
A document in which the student formally accepts a job offer
boss.ex: 承諾 = consent/acceptance. Companies often ask offer recipients to sign one to confirm they accept the offer.
